blindSummary:
The state/province's religious-law penal code took effect 26 November 2000, prescribing 100 lashes plus up to one year's imprisonment for unmarried persons convicted of consensual same-sex activity, and death for married or previously married offenders. This state/province hosts the country's most active religious-police force, functioning as a parallel arrest authority beyond the secular police. A 2019 implementation study by an international religious-freedom commission used 173 religious-law-court cases from 2017 in this state/province and two neighbouring states/provinces to document operational enforcement.

The unit's standing sits below the national baseline: the additional capital-penalty text, the most active religious-police enforcement layer and the documented religious-law-court caseload justify the gap. It stands above the state/province where a religious-law capital sentence has actually been carried out in a documented case, and above the generic religious-law states/provinces, where enforcement documentation is thinner.
